reviewTitle: Definitely size down, definitely inspect the jacket and definitely don't hesitate to buy this!
reviewText: Took me three tries to get this jacket but thanks to Amazon's easy return policy I finally got it and there's a lot to love about it.  First, I ordered a Large because that's what I wear.  The sleeves are really long to the point there was no way I could keep that size so I exchanged for a Med.  The Med. arrived a couple days later and the zipper was broken.  Not just hard to get on and off as I expected that, but the zipper was literally bent to the point where I had to take the jacket off over my head and pry the zipper enough to finally get it open.  So, returned it, replacement arrived a few days later and it was right as rain.Sleeves are still a tad long but I'm fine with that and there is enough space in the jacket for a sweater underneath for layering.  The washed fabric feels much more broken in than the standard Carhartt which I really appreciate.  While rated a 2 in warmness on their bizarre rating scale, this jacket is extremely warm.  It has been around 30 degrees in my area lately and I get toasty in this thing.  The pockets are great,  The interior left chest zipper packet and right side chest velcro pocket were must haves for me and are a welcome addition.  Also, I ordered the attachable hood here on Amazon for $25.00 bucks.  One of my wants was a jacket that didn't have an attached hood and this is one of the few that Carhartt offers.  It is odd to me that for 25 bucks more they don't just include it with the jacket but whatever.  Zipper is somewhat stiff as others have mentioned but once you find the sweet spot of getting it on, you get the hang of it and it becomes second nature.All in all I really like this jacket and hope that it lasts me a very long time.  4/5 stars simply because I don't just throw out 5 stars unless something really blows me away.  This is technically a 4.5 because it's exactly what I was looking for.  Highly recommended.

reviewTitle: Overall good quality - but damaged, and iffy style choice that is masked in the photos on Amazon.
reviewText: This one just showed up. It used soft Amazon and manufacturer patching, so it was wrinkled to the point that it needed either an iron, or time in a dryer (which incidentally is against the instructions on the tag).Problem: Other reviewers have noticed the patches that are very carefully not shown in the Amazon photos. But when you're looking at the thing...yeah, they're there. Also they stick up enough that they may be a catch-and-tear issue. Mine actually showed up damaged with a tear along a long edge of the patch, showing the interior construction. Replacement is on the way, but the best-case scenario is that it'll be in good condition but with those two ridiculous patches. I may hit a local hobby shop for a #11 X-Acto knife to carefully remove them by cutting the stitches one-by-one. Time-consuming but worth it. It looks like one viewer above has already done just that.So, by all appearances, five stars for the coat itself. Fabric looks good, size is great, coat seems warm with fake fur lining around chest (not the sleeves), fake-fur-lined hood is removable (if a little ridiculously large (which may not be a bad idea if you're already wearing a stocking cap or a hoodie). But. Minus 2 points for REALLY trying to hide those patches in the product photos, plus the item showing up damaged.

So glad I purchased this coat which was delivered so quickly. It arrived just in time for a real cold snap. I'm 76 years old and as many older people, I get cold easily. I live in the south where we are not used to very cold weather, at least not extended cold weather. Right after the coat arrived the night temps were in the teens with day time temps below freezing. We have two dogs that need to be walked separately early mornngs. So, I layered up, put on this coat, gloves and knit boggan and stayed warm for both walks. Maybe that doesn't impress you but I'm very impressed with this coat. It's well made and wind proof, to some degree anyway. Mine does not have a sleeve patch but does have the chest patch. I don't see the problem. Men wear t-shirts with advertisements on them all the time. It's not a big deal. Anyway, if you've taken the time to read this overly wordy review, you know I'm very happy with this coat and certainly recommend it.

reviewTitle: Do order the next size bigger
reviewText: Very comfortable. I ordered the next size larger for my size as I saw this comment in other reviews. It fits great. keeps me warm when walking my dog at night in 30 degree weather.

This is a great jacket for the price.  Zipper is sturdy and cuffs are snug to keep out the wind.  Calling it heavyweight is fine -- but it's not as bulky and heavy as my 23-year old parka (which is still in decent shape), for example.  So, I'd say it provides a lot of warmth for its weight.The handwarmer pockets are big enough for a heavy glove, and the interior pocket has a velcro closure to secure your phone or wallet.The hood is well shaped: it lays down nicely when not in use, and you can mold around your head -- I don't miss having a draw-cord.  It seems pretty secure in the wind as long as you angle it properly.  The fleece lining keeps my head warm when I'm not wearing a knit cap.Fit: I'm 42 chest, and I bought a medium.  I still have room to wear a heavy sweatshirt or sweater under this coat.  I have to say that in temperatures from the mid-20s to high 30s, I don't really need a heavy layer underneath.  Wind resistance is very good.Just started trying Amazon Essentials clothing in the last 8 months, and have been quite satisfied, so far.  This piece seems like another good value, as long as it proves to be durable.

Me: 5'9, 230 lbs. Bought XXL, black. Fit as expected. Reasonably light in weight, not bulky. Could layer a hoodie under the jacket if desired. Arm length good for my 35 arms. Cuffs on sleeves for warmth. Hood: substantial, fleece lined, but no drawstring to tighten in the wind. No drawstring to tighten at the jacket's base either, which was just below my beltline, though little room for cold air to blow up & in given my 40 waist. Two medium sized lined outside diagonal pockets with easy-to-operate YKK zippers. One inside left lined breast pocket that was vertical in orientation with a 2cm Velcro strip closure - I'd have preferred a horizontal orientation so nothing drops out if the Velcro fails. Front closure also used same size YKK zipper as pockets. A flap with 5 snaps could be closed over the zipper for additional warmth. I like how the front zipper rises 2-3 up the neck like a scarf for additional warmth. Fabric sheds water effectively. Entire jacket is polyester/ polyester fiberfill. Machine wash cold, dark colors, delicate cycle - dry on low setting. NO dry cleaning. I have been pleased with my ability to move freely in the coat. I'm comfortable at 30*F, even when the wind chill is in the low 20's. Have not laundered yet - I'm hoping the fiberfill does not shift where I lose any insulating properties. Build quality seems good for a coat this reasonable in cost. Would recommend.

Not too bulky for a puffer coat.  Not designed for a fashion statement but designed for warmth.  For this purpose, the coat does an excellent job.  Most important, the zipper is much better than the typical inadequate zipper found on most winter coats in this price range.  I would buy this again.

reviewTitle: Very nice  order a size up, run small...
reviewText: Warning, when ordering, order one size up as these do run small. Read my whole review!!I just got this today and I must say, this is not a bad flannel coat. I say coat because it fits and wears more or less like a coat instead of a jacket.It's very comfortable to wearcas I've just been wearing it around the house to get a feel for this. I love wearing plaid/flannel shirts and coats/jacket so I'm very accustomed to wearing these.Ok so here are the pros:Very comfortable, love the color and choices of colors, materials seem very good although maybe not too rugged, good to wear out in the cold I suppose if wearing another layer of undershirt, wouldn't wear in place of a winter parka.Cons:Although I think a Large fits me good, I went ahead and just ordered an XL to see the size difference as another reviewer stated these run small. Although I do agree to a degree, the length is a bit short for my liking but isn't a deal breaker.I'm 5'7 with just a tad bit of a stomach (stuck on a temporary desk job) and I think the girth of this coat is just a tiny bit tight but again, not a deal breaker because of my poor choice of eating habit...lol. The breast pocket buttons are not very well stitched in and may fall off at some point in time as the stitching really is weak and not strong. So I suppose the longevity of these buttons will depend on the wearer.The sleeves length are spot on for what I like and am pleased with that. In the pictures I posted, you can see the inside of my hand and outside showing the length is a good fit. Also I was able to take a rear picture showing the length of this coat from behind.The very last thing I was a bit disappointed in...the color. In the listing, the pictures show a crisp sharp image. Not so when you get it. The coat literally has a little bit of a blurry look to it and not that crisp sharp look to the color like you see in the listing. Those familiar with wearing plaids and flannels know what I'm talking about.So, all in all this is not a bad coat, I just think maybe I will order a XL and compare the sizes. I like my flannels and plaids a little big because I carry concealed and those are deciding factors for me in these types of clothing. But if I were to grade this on a 5-Star grading, I'd probably give it a 4.5 just because I was disappointed with the coloring being blurred but that isn't a deal breaker.After wearing this just around the house, I think maybe this probably would fall under a jacket as I am discovering this jacket is a bit thin. But it really is comfortable to wear.Hope this helps...Update: November 13, 2023...Ok so I finally got around to ordering the XL size and I got to admit, this fits waaaay better then the size Large which I did return. Again, this is probably not the kind of jacket/coat to wear out in the freezing cold.This is more or less the kind of jacket to wear during those chilly evenings or day. I am talking maybe early winter before it gets too cold. I'm from Northern Idaho and I am familiar with the harsh winters and some winters are worse then others.If you plan on just wearing this to the store, fine go for it but bring something else too just in case. If you're in the Southern California areas, this is perfect for those winters in that area of the country.I honestly will give this a 5 star as the XL fits me much better. I'm 5'7 at about 189-193lbs with a slight stomach but average build. It's not so tight in the shoulders like the Large was and the sleeves aren't too lose, perfect for me to wear along sleeve thermal Under Armor type wicken shirt which I do wear quite often. Plan to order in other colors. I would place this right up there with Legendary Whitetail brand of these types of jacket/coats which I have quite a few of too...Pictures are of the Large size and not the XL size.Hope this helps...

reviewTitle: Very nice design pattern. Good for Fall weather.
reviewText: I love the look and feel but as far as durability/ruggedness this is not a jacket you want to wear for working in rough dirty environments, the jacket just seems too nice and delicate. For something more suited for a harsh outdoor work environment I would go with a more durable option from a company like Carhart, the downside being it will cost 3-4 times as much. This is a good jacket for walking around in public and looking good on chilly days which is what I wanted. The arm length was very short on the medium I originally ordered.  I'm 5' 8 with medium build and when I bent my arms the sleaves road up to my elbows. I ordered a large and it fits a lot better. I wear it daily now for running errands around town or doing small task outside. This jacket is just not thick enough on its own to stay warm for long in hash winter weather. It was 34 degrees today and a little windy and I could feel the cold seeping through for the short time I was outside. Definitely would want to add another layer underneath it if you plan on being outside on a cold winter day for more than an hour. Other than that, the stitching looks good, zipper, pockets are good, but we'll see how well it holds up after a few wash cycles.

reviewTitle: Cheap Quality, Runs Small In Legs
reviewText: I retired 20 years ago. I have ordered many, many sweat pants and athletic pants over the years. I wear this stuff on a daily basis. Here's my feedback and advice.1. First impression is they are way too thin. You can hold them up to a window and see light thru them. Think of these more as pajama bottoms and not sweats. You can wear them in public tho.2. They are indeed comfortable. The material is soft. It feels descent on the skin (most polyester does).3. The stitching is terrible. This is a manufacturing problem that should not exist. I don't see these lasting 20-30 wash cycles without falling apart.As a rule of thumb ALWAYS order sweats and athletic pants 3x your size. If you plan on being very active with them then consider up to 5x your size and have them hemmed. What you're looking for is air around the legs. That thermal barrier is where the comfort comes from. It's what keeps you warm. These are not blue jeans or suits, so shop for that air gap around the legs. Baggy is better! These are not baggy. Maybe the 5x would be appropriate for most of us. But having their length trimmed and hemming adds a level of concern that shouldn't exist.Outside of the above mentioned I would recommend one last thing. Try to find athletic pants that have a liner. Lined sweats / athletic legs are the most comfortable thing you will ever put on your body. You will never be more comfortable. And look for a thin cotton and polyester blend for the inner liner. These are super, super hard to find. But if you can find them, snag them. You'll thank me.

reviewTitle: A+ for comfort, not meant for warmth
reviewText: TL;DR - insanely comfortable pants well-suited to wear around the house and outdoors as long as it isn’t too cold; they are extremely thin and won’t offer much warmth but I cannot say anything negative about this purchase; worth buying a backup pair for when I wear the . . .  pants . . .off of these pants!One evening last month I put on a pair of warmup pants — THE warmup pants, I had no other — and realized they weren’t all that new when Pope JPII was alive, and the elasticity was gone completely, and there was too much pant material for my frame, and maybe I should retire these.They were fairly heavy, but I live in a sub-tropical climate and hardly ever need anything so heavy.So I bought these because they were rated well and inexpensive compared to other known brands and I was not going to be hassled by the thousands of off-brand options, all of which I regard as a gamble at best and a hassle at worstI am very pleased with my purchase. For context, I am 6’0”, between 160 and 165 lbs depending on the day, and could reasonably be described as long-legged but not drastically so.Size: I bought medium, and they fit me perfectly. Take my height and weight into account in deciding your size. They even might run a hair long, but that could be due to how they sit at my waist.Style: I wear these in and around the house, and need only impress my dog, so these were simple and basic enough that I didn't much care how they look, but the photos are accurate.Comfort: I have achieved maximum comfort permitted by natural pants law, and wear these at all times until I go out during the day, and from after I get home and dress down.Material: The material is very thin and lightweight. I don’t think I would want to be outdoors in temperatures below 60° F for long in these, but that’s not of much concern to me. If you have cooler temperatures often enough  and want something to wear outside, this is not the right option.If this description matches your need, you cannot go wrong with these!

reviewTitle: The Good The Bad The Ugly

THE BAD - While I love draw stings I don't love these drawstrings. What they do is take a length of string and bring the ends together in the back of the pants and sew the ends down. The problem is sometimes they don't get them sewed down very good at all. Some will come loose in the back and when it does it is almost impossible to get the string threaded back through the waist band. THE UGLY - While these are the most comfortable pants you will ever wear they are not durable. Granted the will NOT ball up but if you have to do anything where you are actually working they will wear, snag easily. These pants are very delicate and as long as you are doing no work they will be fine as long as the drawstrings stay sewed.

reviewTitle: I liked the old model better, but these are okay.
reviewText: I cannot say anything is wrong with this item.  I just liked the old model that I bought a few years back.  The current models that I just bought are labeled h46110, h48429, 48431.  The models from three years ago that I still have are ei9759, ei9760 and ei9761.  I don't think that the old model is made any longer.The new ones are made from recycled material.  I have no idea if that matters in term of form or function.  All are 100% polyester.  (I don't think that you can see the model number except on the pants themselves and the packaging, but you can Google it and get accurate results.)I am tall and thin and found that the current version is slightly looser on me than the old one.  I wear a medium.  I bought them online, but I think that a small might be too tight.  The drawstrings are two separate strings like shoe laces, not one loop.They fit okay, but once again, just seemed slightly loose even when I tied the strings.  Still, they are wearable although I might look elsewhere in the future.  The length is good for me with running shoes on.  They come down around ankle.  (I wear prewashed 32x34 jeans which I put in the dryer which definitely shrink a bit despite being prewashed so I am probably closer to a 31x33.)I noticed no shrinkage after a few dry cycles or color running when washing in cold water, medium dryer, but I did wash them separately first to be safe.  The old model was also 100% polyester but seemed to shrink slightly for whatever reason.The stitching in the back is not as attractive in my mind compared to the old model, but I don't know if this matters, especially with darker colors.  It seems like they are constructed differently with an extra piece in the back.  In other words, instead of having one piece connected from the legs to the waist band, there seems to be an additional piece between,  You would never notice a problem if you didn't have the older version, and it certainly is not a reason not to buy them, but since I have the older model, it bothered me a bit.I think that most people would be happy for the price that I paid; but, as seems to happen with everything that I like in this world, they replace it with something that is acceptable but not as good.

reviewTitle: The Soft and Thin ADIDAS Track Pants
reviewText: Exactly what I wanted.  Been wearing these pants in one form or another for over 20 years.  They’re very comfortable.  These ones I got, are the softer material.  It’s not the plasticy nylon type material that wooshes between your thighs when you walk.  It’s the nice and soft variety.  I have had two thicknesses of these pants, these are the thinner material.  If you daily these like I do, then you will probably appreciate this review clearing up exactly what you can expect.On this occasion I got the XL Tall size.  The price was right, so I ordered several pairs in differing colors.  I’ve never tried the tall size.  As far as I can tell they’re roughly the same as standard XL, maybe a little tighter around the thighs.  The pairs I own I’ve had for awhile and maybe they’re stretched out, so maybe it’s the same, but these are definitely tighter around the thigh than the pairs I’ve had for years.  I have large thighs, if you don’t have large thighs, it won’t bother you.  It doesn’t bother me actually, but I can tell they’re a little tighter than normal.  Which is fine, it’s good to have a bit of variety and they’ll probably stretch the older they get.  I just hope they don’t shrink in the wash.  One thing unique about these pants is they typically do not shrink in the dryer.  So the tall aspect of the size, yes they are 2 inches, I believe, longer than your standard XL.  I already dragged the pant cuffs around on the carpet, it’s just a little more noticeable.I think you should be able to see in the pic I attached to my review the fabric of these pants to help aid you in determining what it is you’ll get.I hope that helped out one of my fellow ADIDAS track pants lovers out there.

Not sure if this makes any difference, but it occurs to me it may lessen the 'stretching' of the fabric over time in different directions, which may happen with double-logo socks (swapping each sock back & forth from left foot to right foot after each wash etc). Just a thought.

reviewText: I don't like elastic bands that have to stretch too much and then put too much pressure on my waist and leave a mark when I remove the underwear later. These repeated washing have almost completely removed the chemical odor and they don't seem to be losing as much dye now.  The smell and the dye loss will probably be gone with another few washings.Most importantly, these briefs fit somewhat loosely especially where they surround the thighs.  The pouch gives one's equipment just the right amount of room.  They are very cool and comfortable.  There's no button down fly on them.  Instead they just use the overlapped panel approach which is fine.I can recommend these Fruit of the Loom men's briefs.  But, for maximum comfort, I recommend getting the next larger size than that listed for you actual waist size.  That will assure that the waist band will not leave a mark on your skin after wearing them for hours.  I also recommend hand washing them several times before wearing them for the first time just to make sure you don't absorb any loose dye molecules into your skin and body.

reviewTitle: RL Polo can be some of the best casual wear clothing you can buy
reviewText: I've been buying Polo socks since the '80s. I've tried numerous other brands and frankly, only Polo -- at least for casual wear -- works for me. I have pairs that I have had for 2 decades. They have shrunk and nowhere near as comfortable as they once were, but they aren't worn and are still wearable. As with anything else Polo, if you can avoid the shrinkage, you've got a good product to wear almost indefinitely. They either stay with the same factories that produce their goods or they keep good controls over the factories they use, unlike other brands. The only real issue with Polo can be price and or value, but these socks were well worth it.I also have a set of black socks that are essentially the same. I wear them with my dress pants and shoes. They are a little thick but are very comfortable. I have all but quit wearing anything higher than quarter socks. My pants do not ride up on my leg so quarter socks do not show and take less time to put on (not a huge deal but if I'm running late...).The one thing I must caution everyone with respect to ANY quality clothing, but ESPECIALLY RL Polo: wash on COLD on Delicate (with a light detergent like Woolite) and then dry on VERY low heat (delicate setting if you have it). If they aren't quite dry, finish the cycle on air dry if you have that setting. Never run these clothes on any hot water or anything but the lowest heat setting in your dryer for as short a period of time as possible. Trust me on this. I have clothing from 20+ years ago that I still wear that has been washed and dried at home. I dry clean some things and a lot of people get their laundry done but it is unlikely you'll do that to these socks. If you throw them in the washer on hot and high heat in the dryer, you'll be lucky to get 6 months out of them. I see 15+ years for mine.

Recommend to beginner and intermediate runners/hikers, experts may be willing to pay more money for increase of quality.PROs:- Perfect Fit. IMO I find the mesh to be much more durable than the cloth mesh most sports shoes have these days and much easier to clean, which is essential for anyone like myself, who often hikes or runs in forestry/mud.- Above Average Quality. As for the year timeframe, the 1st set was about 8 months of extreme use, then I purchased a 2nd pair which I've had for about 3 months now. This may seem like a short timeframe to some but for me, I usually have to change shoes every 6 months or less if they are lower quality because they get a lot of mileage and use. I liked them enough to buy that 2nd pair instead of some other brand/model.- Decent Arch Support and Sole Tread. You will find other shoes with the same or better, but I didn't see many that were this cheap in price.- Part of Amazon's Try Before You Buy. Free try-ons. You can take up to 6 days to decide whether to keep/return if you wish, and only be charged if not returned by the 7th day. Day 1 is the day they are delivered.- Uniform in Color. The shoe currently comes in all-black or all-white, including the logo. YMMV but this is a pro for me due to work restrictions requiring all-black shoes, so I can also wear them leisurely at work if I choose (I'm a mechanic). Great for anyone with the same issue, or military, etc.CONs:- Not the most expert/elite quality shoe out there, but will definitely check most people's boxes for average needs, imo.- Cost is higher than one might desire for just simple leisure shoes. But as an avid runner, the price is about average. However, they are usually on sale. My 1st set was around 40% off which dropped it from $70-something to $43, which was worth it for me. 2nd set was about 20% off. Winter holiday seems to be the best time for sales price.- Tread pattern is smooth and circular, instead of rigid and square/triangle, in case that matters to you (in regards to rock climbing etc)Overall I was surprisingly satisfied with this shoe model personally, but your mileage may vary.

I purchased this shoe as well as a pair of the Skecher Afterburn M tennis shoes.  I wanted a dedicated work shoe, because I was going though my shoes pretty quickly from wearing the same pair all the time.  So, being that I had already had two previous pairs of the “Afterburn” shoe, and burned through each of them in just over a year respectively, I decided to get another pair of them and also get a pair of the Cessnock Food Service Shoe strictly for work.  Both pairs of shoes arrived yesterday, and today I wore the Food Service shoe (FSS) to work for the first time.I slipped them on and found them to be a perfect fit.  They are very light weight and comfortable.  Usually, I find new shoes need a few days of wear to break-in until they really conform to the shape of your foot and then begin to fit well, but that wasn’t the case with these FSS shoes; they fit perfectly the moment I put them on.I wore them all day at work and discovered something that really surprised me.  We had a snowstorm today and got about 2” by the time I got to work, and had a good 7” by the end of my shift.  I park outside so of course I have to brush the snow off the car.  After doing so I knocked the snow off my shoes before getting into the car.  I was surprised to see that the snow didn’t stick to the material on top of the shoes, it was as if there was a water repellant in/on the material.  I was sort of wondering why my feet weren’t getting cold while I was cleaning off my car and I guess that explains it.  Another surprise was the fact that these shoes make no sound when walking on a tile floor while having wet soles. reviewTitle: 2023 UPDATE - DANG THEY ENDURED A LOT (A FRESH 2020 REVIEW!!! - Yeah, they're pretty good.)
reviewText: I wanted to leave a review for these shoes specifically because Amazon has a habit of throwing old reviews at the buyer rather than more recent ones. There aren't many with a fair critique, or they resort to omg it sucks/rocks. So, here we go.After years of using TredSafe shoes due to just not having the money to afford fancy-shmancy, I bit the bullet on these shoes figuring I could at least default to other shoes if they didn't work out. Also, a lot of reviews complained on durability and such, but they were recommended, so I went for it.Durability: Uhhhh, folks must have run over their pairs with a lawn mower to get them wrecked like they were, because wow have mine been accidentally kicked into and scraped by a LOT of old metal equipment and hardware with basically no damage. Really, the only damage was a screw I somehow stepped on, drilling a hole into the bottom. I mean, it didn't poke my foot, so no harm done.Comfort: Okay, so memory foam is a big your mileage may vary situation, but generally the foam is pretty okay in these shoes. Seeing as I run around a lot more at my new job than I did my old one, these do pretty good at cushioning my 13W feet. Then again, I am also a tall dude, so the memory foam cushioning may not be as effective for me. It hasn't been long enough to really wear it out either, but again, your mileage may vary. Also depends on whether you really understand memory foam, which I kind of don't. I might be totally off-base.But anyways. Even without that, the general feel and support of the shoe is good. The fact that my heels basically never hurt after eight-hour shifts when they would tend to hurt in the old, cheap TredSafe shoes is a pretty good testament to that fact.The fit: It fits...? I mean, 13W feet, I bought 13W. It fit pretty much as expected. The only minor complaint I can make is more a special case: there isn't a lot of room for inserts. See, I'm weird and have a tendency to put more pressure on the front of my feet than the heel, and not a shoe can be found at reasonable price for someone weird like me. I'd like to be able to fit some front support into the shoes to counter that, but there's just not enough room. Maybe once I wear out the memory foam, but otherwise... Well, that's a me thing. If you walk like a normal person rather than like I did as a kid to catch late-night TV without being caught, then you should be okay.Other stuff: One other minor complaint is just a typical sneaker issue but a bit worse. When the bottoms of the shoes get wet, walking on any kind of hard floor gives off an obnoxious squeaking sound. I don't mean like basketball court squeaking. I mean like twisting leather squeaking. To be fair... They're sneakers. They'll make noise like that, but it's usually not that annoying. They do dry out pretty quick so long as you don't keep getting them wet, so it doesn't last particularly long.So... Four stars? Yeah. They're pretty good overall, and they sure do take a beating. I keep expecting something I do to rip it open, but there isn't a single tear or crack anywhere (besides the hole from the screw). Main problem is just memory foam getting in the way of using inserts, lack of front foot support for those like yours truly, and the obnoxious wet squeak. Still a solid shoe, though. Worth the money.Update: 07/22/2023Just bought a second pair because the pair I use finally showed signs of serious wear, which is pretty impressive since I've used these shoes for almost everything from job work to yard work. They have had their soles handed to them regularly and only just now started actually falling apart in any measure. They aren't dead just yet, but the shoes were on a good sale so I bought pair two ahead of time.I did end up wearing out the memory foam rather quick (but I also walk weird, so once again your mileage may vary) but pulling them out to replace with new inserts was really easy, so it was a simple swap-out. I will say it's best to just swap for more memory foam since other support inserts didn't help just because of the shoe's own support.So yeah, running back in to say you REALLY have to try to destroy these shoes to make them fall apart: for having lasted 3 years of me, they've done a very good job staying together. They're still comfortable, pretty good support, and make the annoying leather-twisting noise when wet, but I definitely think they're worth the price, sale or not.

reviewTitle: I'm disappointed in the advertising message on the tongue of the shoe, but these are very good shoes
reviewText: I've been wearing Brooks Adrenaline GTS shoes for 8 years, and during that time have bought multiple pairs of 3 different models of GTS shoes.  They are really good shoes, very comfortable, I can very easily wear then all day long (more comfortable than just wearing socks around the house), and perfect for the particular pronation of my feet.  However, this is the first time I've purchased the 2024 edition of these shoes (the Adrenaline GTS 24), and I'm disappointed to discover that there is now a conspicuous advertising message on the tongue of the shoes.  In a bold black stripe, it says Adrenaline 24 GTS, which is eye-catching and detracts from the appearance of the shoes.  On the GTS 18 and GTS 16 models of these shoes, the branding on the tongue of the shoe was very subtle, which I like.  But with these GTS 24 shoes, it's kind of like wearing a big NIKE message on the front of my shirt or something.  Part of the reason I chose this un-flashy gray color is so my shoes will blend in with any casual outfit I wear, but with these shoes, I feel like I'm making a big statement to the world that I love my Brooks Adrenaline GTS shoes.  The bold black stripe is made of a spandex material, and is only sewn-in on the ends of the stripe, so I guess I could use some scissors to cut it off.  But then there would be this little messy black edge where I cut off the advertising.  Anyway, bummer about the bold black advertising stripe, and I hope they omit this in future models of this shoe.  But it's still a really good shoe.

At a certain point in life, a man reaches a deeper understanding.  A viewpoint that permanently alters his worldview, and makes him question all that came before.  This can happen slowly, as experience and knowledge grows, and ultimately crystalizes around a kernel of this new perspective.  Or it can happen suddenly, in an epiphany of recognition that forces a foundational frame of reference adjustment.  Yesterday I experienced the latter, and I wanted to share it in case any of you have yet to reach a similar point.  As enter the fall of life, I feel compelled to offer this new personal world order in the hope that you may benefit longer than I will likely enjoy.While this change thunder-struck me suddenly yesterday, some background will help put the revelation in proper context.  It all started with the bankruptcy of Sears.  Sears engaged in a foolhardy acquisition strategy during the 1980's of retail and non-retail businesses that would be completely undercut by the digital revolution of the 1990's.  The debt accumulated from these various acquisitions would drag on company financial statements for decades as revenues slowly eroded to online shopping alternatives.  Finally, in the face of an unmanageable October 2018 debt payment of $134 million, Sears declared Chapter 11.  Eddie Lampert made several attempts to secure funding for a reorganization strategy, but they would all ultimately fail.  None of this impacted me until the end of 2019 when the last Sears in Jacksonville closed.At that point I had a shoe problem.  For decades I had purchased brown four-hole lace-up suede loafers from Sears.  They were a store brand that sold for $30 or $40.  I had probably purchased a dozen or more pair of these.  I would often buy two or three pair at a time so I wouldn't need to return to the store so often as they wore out.  But now Sears and my default shoe choice were gone!  Panic ensued.  I started searching the internet for the manufacturer of this shoe which I had enjoyed for so many years.  The hope was that another distribution channel would emerge, or that a transition to online sales could be found.  No luck.  So at the dawn of COVID-19, I was facing an existential shoe crisis.It was about March 2020 when my last trusty Sears loafers were at end-of-life.  Most real world retail was shuttered, and supply chain disruption was in full force.  There were no shoes to buy.  Finally, a local Rack Room reopened and I scoured the shelves for a suitable replacement.  I eventually settled for a deck style shoe that was only mildly stylistically objectionable, but seemed acceptably comfortable as one of the very few models offered in wide width.  For nearly two and a half years this daily worn (weekday) pair of shoes sustained me.  Last week I was forced back to the retail experience for a hopefully improved selection of casual shoe options.Did I find an improved post-COVID selection?  Hell no, I did not!  It was WAY worse.  There were no wide offerings at all!  Three shoe store visits left me cursing the pathetic state of IRL retail, and the stupid business people who were essentially forcing me to shop online.  So home to Amazon I went, with the name of an untried shoe brand and model seen in a store.  It was a pleasing looking set of footwear that I was going to gamble might be suitable.  And the size variety available on Amazon was breathtaking.  All the sizes I was familiar with, that were completely missing from any store, were available with a click.  I don't know when stores decided that they couldn't offer size selection.  They certainly did in the 1970's!  How did they lose that ability?  Anyway, shoes selected and ordered online with delivery anticipated in a couple days.  Fine.Ladies and gentleman, this is it.  These Rockport Oxford Eureka Walking Shoes are THE most comfortable shoes I have ever owned...bar none.  I am gobsmacked by how comfortable these shoes are.  Eureka is right!  I think back to pre-Rockport me and shake my head in sorrow.  Poor fella.  Stuck in a rut of frugally driven brick-and-mortar retail based consumption resulting in the bare minimum of utility.  Not even guessing about the possibility that such a paradigm shift could be out there.  Who knows what might have been if that version of me had found these shoes earlier?  Years of an improved outlook on life is the most obvious missed opportunity.  Perhaps he would have turned to philanthropy?  Trying to engineer life improvements for those around him in an effort to induce similar outlook-altering reactions in society's less fortunate?  I literally skipped around the house yesterday sharing the good news with my family.  I haven't skipped since a 1973 visit to Cedar Point with my Aunt Fran.  Eureka my friends.  Eureka indeed.  If you're in need, I beg you to give these shoes a try.  If I can convince just one of you, then this lunchtime prose will have been worth it.Edit: Two year update on durability - These spectacular shoes have been part of my workday fit for two years now.  No major durability issues to report.  The highest wear was on the insole.  The soles still have quite a bit of life, and are still well attached to the uppers.  One black pair I bought has fully thrown their insoles, and the brown pair have significantly worn insoles.  I still feel that this wear pattern is above average compared to my past shoe purchases.  So much so, I just ordered another pair of both black and brown Rockport Oxford Eureka Walking Shoes.  Love 'em, and looking forward to the fresh kicks!

reviewTitle: Great, long lasting, very durable shoes.  Break-in required.
reviewText: These are awesome shoes.  They last for a very long time.  They run a bit tight, and pretty stiff.  I use old-school techniques, that I learned in the Army, for new Rockports.  I put them on, and wear them for an hour.  I'm not going to lie, they chew on my feet pretty hard for that hour.  Then I wear them for a couple of hours, on some errands that require walking.  They start out biting pretty hard, but after a couple of hours, they feel like a good pair of gloves, and they're like walking on clouds.  The third time, I wear them to work.  I pack a spare pair of shoes, in case my feet get too sore, but they usually don't.  After that third day, they might be a little hard to put on, but once on, they're super comfortable.  I have a pair that are 5 years old, still look great for office work, and are one of two pairs of shoes that I go to when I know I'm going to be on my feet a lot.  It's a process to break them in, but good leather requires break in.  These shoes are worth it!

This might not be brief, but it will be efficient (and worth it)!1. I bought/tried these shoes because, within six months, I have always ripped the front of my new balance shoes (for ~ a decade) requiring new ones. Hence I waited 1 year + to write this review...2. These shoes are as comfortable as new balance and still look new! So no need to constantly replace them... Or baby them (I'm hard on shoes).As you can imagine the steel keeps the front of the shoe from ripping. So never again...3. I run (with my dog -- fast) in these shoes, they are that comfortable.4. Therefore they are perfect from a security perspective. Not only can no one stomp on your foot and do you harm, but imagine getting kicked with these suckers on! Also, you could run away if you needed to...5. These shoes are so comfortable, I routinely think I'm wearing my slippers and thus fail to swap them when I get home. I've caught myself many times realizing I wore them all day.6. I made a mistake when I bought my first pair. I knew I would get lazy and not change shoes to walk my dog, so I wanted to avoid smashing my toes against the steel plate during a run. If you're a runner of any distance, you know how much damage that can do to your feet. So I bought 10s instead of 9.5. Four months later I bought 9.5 because they clearly accounted for that in the design. And the 10s were too big. My feet were sliding around too much in those, even with pads in them.7. They are roomy vertically so I doubled up some pads in them (the 9.5s) thus increasing their comfort. Yet they remain roomy/comfortable. I never bump up against the plate.8. You can put HEAVY things on them, I often hang drywall, and you can set it on your shoes feeling no pressure on your feet while keeping the drywall off the ground.9. They are a tad on the warm side. Terrific in winter, and even good for walking in snow, but in the summer, on a hot day my feet will sweat. Not wonderful. They breathe, but there are tradeoffs. IE It's hard to breathe through a steel plate. So I can't blame the manufacturer, I still love them.10. The sole is not particularly flexible, it doesn't exactly conform/bend to your feet during a run, but I wouldn't think buyers of shoes like these would care.  I got used to it, but it's worth mentioning in case others might (care). And that leads to my next point:11. During a run, a sharp rock came up through the bottom of my first pair. I was shocked because that never happened before. And I suspect the ridgidness of the sole may have contributed. They weren't destroyed by that, but if you're walking around a construction site, be careful. Safe on top, not so sure about the bottom. In a year + that hasn't happened with this pair. They're not bad soles, but perhaps the only room for improvement.12. I never thought someone stomping on my foot could do me harm. I thought that was ridiculous in movies until I dropped something heavy on my foot 2 years ago. Wow - ouch! So even if you don't do construction, these are a great upgrade to your personal security for that reason alone.13. Even with the steel plate and sturdy construction, I don't find them all that heavy (anymore), but they are heavier and a bit clunky, runners will notice and it took some getting used to. Eventually my laziness, about changing shoes, won out and now I'm used to running in them. And I no longer view them as such a drag. For several months, I loathed running in them until one day I just forgot.14. I don't consider them waterproof. Water resistant maybe, but don't sell your waders. Your feet will get wet if you submerge them.15. If you want shoes that will last forever, look good without maintenance, increase your personal security, protect your feet, and that you will eventually find very comfortable, these are for you.

reviewTitle: Good, solid, comfortable shoes but very, very heavy.
reviewText: I got tired of my normal athletic shoes going bad from the stress of daily use on the job, so I went looking under the search term durable work shoes.  (Looking via Duck and Swisscows and Qwant, mind you, not via Amazon's own search fields, which, inexplicably, continue to be left as almost 100% useless.)Inevitably, nothing that was classified as a.) a shoe and b.) durable was available without a steel toe, so I relented and bought these.  For the record:  The heaviest thing I'm likely to drop on my feet is a disk of Lanthanum/Telluride alloy (or maybe Silicon/Germanium,) that's roughly the size, shape and weight of a U.S. Nickel, so I'm not really in need of steel-toed shoes.  But if you want durable, apparently you have to get the Medieval Class toe box, so I just bought them.I don't know if it's just the steel toe or a combination of that and the heavier-duty rubber and upper material, but these shoes are seriously heavy.  Not a big problem if you like the added exercise, but it would be great if shoe manufacturers would offer a version of the exact same work shoe with all of the exact same materials, but without the mëtal hardware.  But I knew that going in so...These are excellent shoes despite the weight.  I have wide feet and they're available in EE width (if they hadn't been I simply would not have bought them, because you can't be cool if your feet are uptight, as the old Hush Puppies ad used to say.)  They're built like tanks but are perfectly comfortable nonetheless, and I'm on my feet roughly 80% of every nine-hour workday.I got my normal size and width, and even with a pair of podiatrist-prescribed orthotic inserts and Odor-Eater pads, they fit perfectly.  When I put them on in the morning the toe areas do feel tight, but the inserts settle within minutes and they're a perfect fit thereafter.  So be aware that if you do not use any kind of insert these might be a little roomy.  The laces are also heavy-duty and the eyelets for them allow you to tighten them without messing with the loop-by-loop finger-pull thing - but neither do they let loose too easily - all of which I like lots.Given the excellent price, durability and fit, I'm really happy that I picked these.  Time will tell how well they'll hold up, but I've been wearing them on the job for two months and they still look and feel brand-new. I'm on hands and knees and crawling into the guts of systems and lab equipment frequently, and though the inevitable dirt is there, I don't even see so much as a scuff on the outer surfaces, anywhere.  Good shoes, if seriously heavy in the weight class.

reviewTitle: Great work shoes for construction, warehouse jobs, etc
reviewText: Great for working in a warehouse. Very protective. I can kick heavy stuff without hurting my foot if I curl my toes slightly. I've used my shoes to avoid pinching my fingers when setting down heavy objects, to get pallet jacks unstuck from pallets by holding the pallet in place with my foot, and to get old rusty latches on delivery vans open by kicking the lever. I know from experience that the steel toe can support over 1,000lbs, just don't tell my boss how I figured that out....I'm not sure how protective they are when it comes to stepping on nails, but I'll let update my review if I find out! (Stepping on nails sticking up out of boards isn't exactly a rare occurrence in warehouse and construction environments)They're surprisingly water resistant. Stepping in puddles, walking through snow, and even pressure-washing vehicles doesn't get my feet wet. They're quite grippy, and the tread on the soles doesn't seem to wear down. While wearing these, I've only ever slipped on ice and soapy concrete, never on wet wood, concrete floor, metal, etc.They're certainly not comfort shoes, but they're comfortable enough for work. Better than broken toes! They're not light, but they don't feel particularly heavy. I'm still fairly agile while wearing them, they're not great for running, but I can run in them comfortably and without tripping. It's quite comfortable to rest one foot on top of the other while sitting, since the shoes don't bend too easily like sneakers do.They're very durable, aside from the memory foam insoles, which develop holes pretty quickly, although you really can't feel the holes. In my experience, they last about 8 months, which is decent, considering they're relatively inexpensive and stand up to a lot. My first pair had a bit of peeling rubber on the front and the holes in the insoles had gotten quite deep, so I replaced them, although they're still wearable as a backup option. I just bought replacements for my second pair, which are actually in pretty good shape other than the inside of the left shoe wearing down, causing the hard protective layer inside to rub on my heel and cause minor discomfort while walking.The sizing seems accurate. I have fairly wide feet, and wear size 13 in most brands, sometimes 14 (eg, Under Armour). The size 13-Wide fits perfectly, with just enough room for my toes to not be squished together like they are in most shoes.9/10, would recommend these for anyone with the risk of injuring their feet at work.

reviewTitle: Perfect, even if you are short
reviewText: I was a bit hesitant about purchasing this dress online, especially when it comes to sizing. I’m 5 feet tall, 160 pounds with a bit of a gut, and I really didn’t want to end up looking like a round blob or have my boobs spilling out. I also wanted to find something that would cover my arms and stomach because I’m not a fan of showing those areas. This dress turned out to be exactly what I was hoping for! It fit perfectly and had the flowy sleeves I was looking for, offering great coverage without feeling bulky.The length was perfect for my height—just grazing the top of my feet when I wore wedges. If it’s a little long for you with wedges, the waist is constructed in a way that you can pull it up slightly to shorten the dress a tad more. The dress is a beautiful pink color, and I received lots of compliments throughout the day, which made me feel so pretty.One thing I wasn’t thrilled about was that the bottom was a bit sheer, with a slit that exposed more than I was comfortable with, especially since I have spider veins and prefer to keep my legs covered. I had no trouble taking it to my local seamstress, and for just $7, she sealed up the slit for me, which was an easy fix.The dress does come with a built-in slip, but I added a shorter slip underneath to avoid a Princess Di moment—especially since it was an outdoor wedding...just in case. Overall, this dress was the perfect choice for me. I felt confident, comfortable, and, most importantly, pretty!

Let’s start with what I love….the color is beautiful and it fits true to size. I’m 5’4, 38B cup & 140 pounds.  I have a lot of saggy fat in my stomach. Tbh, I could pass as a pregnant woman. This is probably the 20th dress I’ve ordered this month looking for different options to wear to a wedding, shower and rehearsal. Most of the dresses with the leg slit are more immodest than what I like, so those have all gone back.  This slit hits my calf, even when I sit in doesn’t ride up and show off the lady parts. It’s not so sheer that a slip is required and it hides my gut so well I won’t have to wear any slimming tank or body suit underneath. The only negative, the snap is just not placed well. I wear a Warner bra from Kohls. It’s the only brand bra I can wear that doesn’t push my under arm fat up uncomfortably. It smooths the back fat. I have a few, with and without underwire and Extra padding. But with a 38 B cup most dresses, even when paired with a bra with no padding or underwire, typically is tight in the bust. This dress gives plenty of bust room but again; the snap hits in the wrong area. It causes a gape in the material that looks awkward and ill fitting. Thankfully my mother in law was able to remove the snap easily and just do a bit of hand sewing to tack the dress In a more flattering spot right above the bra line. My video shows the snap undone with a pin tacking it together where she will sew it shut. If you have a 38B cup and don’t have anyone that can alter this dress it may not work for you. If your really small busted than I’d say go for it, as the spot the snap sits would be fine for you. If your really large busted I’d also say the snap would work since your filling this entire area with boob and there won’t be a gape in the dress like it did for me. I will definitely be ordering another color, most likely the yellow flor, because the quality of this dress is great. This coming from someone who has tried on over 30 dresses from Amazon in the last 2 weeks and knows what’s crap vs. quality. I love this dress!

My big complain about this is the uneven hem! The dress was significantly longer on one side -which I somehow did not catch when I quickly tried it on. Not an option to return because I removed the tags and washed prior to wear. I used a safety pin to get me through the night, but I am going to take it to be altered (may even see if the slit up the front can be made a little longer). It’s comfortable. It’s cute. Just some obvious quality control issues.

reviewTitle: Great fit for gym-rat waist and quads, but tight in the calf area
reviewText: These jeans fit like the proverbial glove in the waist / glute / thigh area, but I have genetically huge calf muscles (even without working them in the gym,) and the cut of these jeans is fairly tight from the knee downward.  They'll stretch with use of course, so I can still wear them, but if I were going to do a Rev B on these I'd take into account the fact that people who are gym rats will also work their calves. Which means a bit more circumferential span is needed there.They don't need much of a tweak - else you'd end up with lower legs that are relaxed-fit-baggy - but maybe another inch in total circumference at the calf. When I bend down for something and stand back up these ride up my calves and stick there, I've suddenly got the Pee-Wee Herman high-water style and have to pull them back down.Not a big deal though. Again they *will* stretch, they are still an excellent fit, they're inexpensive, they're available in a solid, dark indigo dye. Call me strange but I'm not enthused at the idea of buying jeans that look like they've been pre-worn for six months by a garage mechanic with a serious incontinence problem. If there's some kind of perceived stylishness in jeans that are visibly worn, buying them pre-stressed is as lame as buying a guitar with the paint pre-worn.  Like Oh, dig ME, I've used these so intensely that the paint is worn off.  Except... umm, not really.  No.  Just... no. Best of all these are available in 28 length on 32 waist, which eliminates a big peeve of mine vis-à-vis jeans:Manufacturers sell pants based on waist vs. inseam measurements, and while the waist measurement is a definite thing, the inseam is not.  Tailors typically measure your inseam from the point of direct contact with your groin down to your ankle.  So think about it, or better yet just stand up right now and check this out: When you're standing, whatever pants you're wearing do *not* magically stay snugged right up to your Naughty Bits. Rather, the actual cross-seam where the inseam starts will generally hang at least an inch or two *below* the actual, physical surface of your body from which the inseam usually gets measured.Which means - sur-vey SEZ? - the pants you buy with your tailor-measured inseam will be too long, and you're going to be walking around on top of that last inch of cuff, cursing the fact with every step.  Unless you go to the expense and hassle of having them altered after the fact. So... a selection of inseam dimensions that actually matches people's true pant-leg length!  Amazing!  The only thing Amazon - and the whole of the garment industry - could do better is offer men's jeans with those tailor-assumption-inseam options extending all the way down to 26 or 27.  We're not all bean-poles out here. I would argue that the vast majority of men, at least in N. America, are shorter than the garment industry weirdly assumes.I'm writing this before having done a wash and with only a day's wear, so I can't comment on how durable the dye is.  But at least it's at an intense, deep blue as a starting point - and assuming the dye is of decent quality that's the best you can ask for.[Update 07-27-24: All of the above applies - still a good pair of jeans - but I'm not happy with how the dye is fading. There's a serious fade on both the front and back of the thighs but nowhere else, so the result is that cheesy two-tone thing that screams Dig these bargain jeans I got from K-Mart!  I probably won't be buying more of these until (unless) I start seeing raves about how this problem - and the calf-size problem - have been corrected in a Rev. B.]

reviewTitle: Comfort and Style: A Great Alternative to Birkenstocks!
reviewText: I recently bought the KIDMI Women's Suede Clogs Leather Mules Cork for my 12-year-old daughter, and she absolutely loves them! My daughter wears them to school, on walks, and just lounging at home, and they never seem to hurt or cause discomfort—something I really appreciate. The suede upper gives them a more polished, versatile look, which works well with both casual outfits and a bit more dressed-up styles.What’s also great is how easy they are to slip on and off—perfect for a busy tween who’s always on the go. I wore these clogs just about every day since I got them and they are still holding up amazingly. The suede wipes off easily. I have zero complaints about these shoes, I'm planning to buy another pair in the near future. These are an awesome, affordable alternative to higher end, more expensive clogs and are the same quality and style.

(I work three to four 12hr shifts/week.)Here's why, I like a soft padded foot bed, particularly at my heels. These are abundantly padded. reviewTitle: If you have wide feet, size UP!
reviewText: If you’re reading this, size up a half size when purchasing! These run SMALLER than previous glycerin models!I have always been a size 6.5 WIDE in Brooks and have had several previous “Glycerin” models, so I was very surprised when 6.5 wide was not only too small but too NARROW. I sized up to a 7, and it fits much better.That being said, Brooks is stepping up their game in terms of the style and colors of their shoes. In my opinion, the Glycerin 21 is the most attractive shoe I’ve owned from brooks and the first that doesn’t somewhat resemble “old people shoes”. Looks aside, I will say that I like the fit of the previous model — Glycerin 20 — a bit better. The bottom of the shoes are very padded and heavier like Hokas, which is great for walking but not the best for running.Overall, Brooks is still the best option out there in terms of comfort and traction. reviewTitle: Great for walking/everyday wear; nice size selection
reviewText: After giving birth, I needed to get rid of pretty much all of my shoes because my feet got longer by a half size.I went to a sport shoe store and got a white pair of these and LOVED them. They are so comfy, provide me the right amount of arch and foot support. I come from a family where the women have larger than average foot size, so finding shoes can be difficult for me. Brooks offers a really nice size range, so it’s not too hard for me to find shoes that fit and are actually cute.For what I needed, these seem like they will be very durable, which is just daily walking and running around after a toddler.I got the purple color from Amazon when they had a little bit of a sale. I’m not typically a “need the same shoe in different colors” kind of person, but these shoes are just that good, in my opinion.

The Brooks Glycerin has been my go-to sneaker for years. I’ve already been professionally fitted a few times and this is usually the winner, so I wasn’t buying blind. I’d been squeezing the last bit of life out of my 20s when faced with the decision of going for the 21s or the new 22s. The 21s were marked down due to the release of the 22s, but it’s all about comfort. Several running reviews guided me to the 21s over the 22s. I’ve got about 85 miles on them so far and I love them. Bonus points for an ultra bright color with top notch reflective elements. These are not a fast shoe but they’re great for anyone looking for a neutral shoe that’s comfortable enough for long distances. As is true with most premium running shoes, they are good to go straight out of the box. They also work for just standing around. I have a work desk that can be raised to standing height and these keep me comfortable when I choose to stand for an hour or two.

reviewTitle: The best general tennis shoes/walking shoes of my life
reviewText: I was a bit hesitant to order these shoes because I've myself never heard of Brooks. I took them out of the box and thought That is a really thick sole. And then I put them on my feet and I was thrilled nearly 100%.Pros- The regular width shoe is perfect for someone who has a generally skinny foot but a slightly wider ball of foot area. This has been a challenge for my entire life and I've often had to either buy wide shoes that make my feet swim or have shoes that are too tight around my toes and ball of my foot.- The toe area is long enough over center to accommodate those of us with a long second toe, or Greek toe. This can be especially helpful if you suffer pain or potential hammer toe due to cramped shoes. My other toes feel supported and don't feel like they're swimming, but my long toe also has plenty of room and support.- The cushy support from the nitrogen injected spongey soles is something I never knew I needed.- The arch support feel fantastic for high arches. I didn't even feel the need to switch out the insole.- The top of the shoe is stretchy and breathable.- I have felt comfortable and supported since I started wearing these about a week ago. I had major foot surgery in 2021 and have had issues with my feet and toes ever since. These don't solve all those problems but I feel a lot better. I didn't feel like I could comfortably walk 10,000 steps per day and now I do. I'm going over 13,000+ per day.- They were easy to wear even without breaking in. I've had only minimal breaking in pains and that is a really big deal for me because that's never been the case before.Cons- The shape and height of the heel back on this shoe rubs into my heel, not just on the bridge but on the sides as well. This meant that I had to buy socks with a heel tab on them. I am not a huge fan of those kinds of socks because they are always super thick. This means that a lot of the glorious room I got in these shoes was then taken away from me by thick socks that I didn't even want to buy. So just remember that if you buy these shoes you now also have to buy $20 of socks.- The shoelaces are not typical for tennis shoes and they're the kind of tubular ones. This means that they are harder to untie and more likely to get stuck in annoying knots.- I had to relearn to walk in these shoes. The sole is so thick and springy that walking is not intuitive at first. I fell off my walking pad the first time I used it with these shoes.Overall, these are really great shoes and I highly recommend them.

I knew from the get go these were the winners. For reference I usually wear a 7 but sometimes a 6.5 and the 7 were great. I also have a bit of a higher arch. I walk about 12 miles a week so they get used! These will be my go to shoes now. I can also run errands after in these and still look good.

reviewText: We purchased several packs of these onesies for our newborn, and indeed, onesies proved to be the go-to outfit for hanging out at home and for layering when we go out. The more I thought about it, after washing and wearing the 6 or so pair I had kept, I had kept, I recalled seeing  a picture of Amazons jeans for petite women, on one of the pages where I had ordered the jeans I now had. I decided to give them a try. I purchased 2 pair, as that would give me more jeans than I needed, but a little bit of summery color. They came today. reviewTitle: Proper measurement makes for flattering jeans
reviewText: I always start out saying that measuring tape doesnt lie.This brand is Lee. Like most brands, they have their own size chart. Also this particular style won't flatter all figures... Especially if you choose a size too small. So measure yourself, and look at the sizing guide. Theres a bit of a trick to it (not really).I like:1.The material of these jeans is soft and has some stretch to it but its not suffocating in warmer weather.2. The high waist is perfect height.3. They give the perfect silouhette (like wide legs pants/jeans circa 1930s-1950s) *as long as you get the correct size for YOUR measurements.*My height and weight cannot help you decide your own size. Why? You might ask.I AM 5'4. My measurements taken with a seamstress tape at various times of the year:Fullest part of bust with bra on: 35-37Waist at navel: 25-27Hips:35-37My legs and arms are a bit lengthy and my shoulders are broad. I have to buy larger shirts just because of my shoulders for some brands.Someone with the same height and and weight as myself might have a larger bust, a smaller waist and hips than mine. And they would need a smaller size of these jeans and wear larger size shirts.Or if a person is a pear figure they might need a larger size while their shirt size would likely ve smaller than mine.  Even if we weigh the same we need different sizes. Get it? Good.I purchased the 2 short. Why?1. Im 5'4.2. My waist measures 26 most of the time.3. My hips measure 37 most of the time.Usually when jeans are sized they shouldnt be the exact same measurement as the body. They should provide an extra inch or so to accomodate for tucking in your shirt a d fitting over undergarments.I had a suspicion that Lee would factor that into the sizes... They did.The jeans add 1.5 inches to accomodate and they call it size 2 (i guess for vanity's sake?). While the EU size us 26 (an actual size 6 according to classic garment making). They are stretchy so the fit is a little more forgiving than a non stretch alternative. However these jeans are not the same as skinny jeans. Youre not supposed to squeeze into them.For that perfect silhouette, you really must pay atrention to your waist AND hip measurements. If the difference between your waist and hips is greater than 15 i.e. You're a wasp waist hourglass (i kind of envy you guys), or a wasp waist pear: you want to make sure these are the right fit for your hips first.  Thet should give that extra 1-1.5 according to the chart, or even get a size up. After you get them you could take them to a tailor to custom fit the waist (if you got a perfect hip size) and the hip area to perfection (thats where the larger size comes in) and these would look SUPER AMAZING on you.A banana figure may need a small adjustment at the waist or hips. They could possibly size down if their hips and waist have a very small difference since the material stretches.If you have an apple or inverted triangle figure, you should pay the most attention to your waist size. If necessary, you can also have the hips adjusted to improve the line if your silhouette.Final thoughts: i am happy that I can find wide leg jeans easier now. Before, i would just make do with boot cut jeans (i like those a lot too). I had to wait a while for them to come back in style (jeans at least). However, i dont think it should be like this. Jeans arent supposed ti be like this! Different jeans flatter different figures in various ways. For instance an inverted triangle figure might have a more striking silhouette in a set of jeans with a harem pant fit,  or a Monroe style jean. Both would balance out the shoulder line quite well. An apple body would probably rock some bell bottoms like a champ by highlighting slender thighs and having the bell to balance their upper body.Each figure can create the perfect silhouette for their personality and figure. So... Look at all the various jean styles available and choose whats best for YOUR body and personality.After all comfortable clothes that compliment our figures are always the best!

reviewText: I like:- Soft denim fabric- Feels cool in summer- No tears - you can diy your own artNo fading - no fake slimming illusion- Stretches but not slimming panel or coloring- Can add your own decorations and style or leave it plain-Nice height on the waist.- Can dress up or down.Nothing not to like.Apple shape would need to size up one to two sizes. I was a bit skeptical to get these because of the mixed reviews, but I'm glad I did. The black is a true dark black and the material is incredibly forgiving. Based on other reviews, I think the jean style depends heavily on your body type.I'm 5'6, ~180 lbs, and typically a 10/12 in most brands. According to the size chart, I am a 14 so I ordered that.
